subproblem.title: Leibniz bound for determinants: |det A| ≤ n!·c^n when every entry satisfies |A_ij| ≤ c
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, c ∈ ℝ, and let A = (A_{ij})_{i,j ∈ Fin n} be a real n×n matrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) with |A_{ij}| ≤ c for all i, j ∈ Fin n. Then |det A| ≤ n!·c^n. For n = 0 the empty determinant is 1 = 0!·c^0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), (∀ i j, |A i j| ≤ c) → |Matrix.det A| ≤ (n.factorial : ℝ) * c ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(b) of the supplied proof of the selected node (“By the Leibniz formula and the triangle inequality, an n×n matrix whose entries are bounded by C in absolute value has |det| ≤ n!·C^n (prove this from Matrix.det_apply; Matrix.det_le is not imported)”), written out in full.

Notation. S_n := Equiv.Perm (Fin n) is the group of permutations of Fin n. sgn(σ) ∈ ℤˣ = {1, −1} is the sign of σ; it acts on ℝ by multiplication by ±1.

1. (Leibniz formula, Matrix.det_apply.) det A = Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} sgn(σ) • Π_{i ∈ Fin n} A_{σ(i), i}.
2. (Triangle inequality, Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs.) |det A| ≤ Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} |sgn(σ) • Π_i A_{σ(i), i}|.
3. (Removing the sign.) Fix σ ∈ S_n. By Int.units_eq_one_or, sgn(σ) = 1 or sgn(σ) = −1. So sgn(σ) • y is y or −y, and |sgn(σ) • y| = |y| for every real y. The absolute value is multiplicative on finite products (Finset.abs_prod), so |Π_i A_{σ(i), i}| = Π_i |A_{σ(i), i}|. Hence the σ-summand in step 2 equals Π_i |A_{σ(i), i}|.
4. (Bounding each product.) For every i ∈ Fin n, the hypothesis applied to the entry in row σ(i), column i gives |A_{σ(i), i}| ≤ c; also 0 ≤ |A_{σ(i), i}|. Finite products of nonnegative reals are monotone in each factor (Finset.prod_le_prod₀, whose hypotheses are exactly these two facts). So Π_{i ∈ Fin n} |A_{σ(i), i}| ≤ Π_{i ∈ Fin n} c = c^n, by Finset.prod_const and card (Fin n) = n. For n = 0 both products are empty and equal 1 = c^0, so no sign condition on c is used.
5. (Counting permutations.) By steps 2–4, |det A| ≤ Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} c^n = card(S_n)·c^n. By Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin, card(S_n) = (card (Fin n))! = n!. Therefore |det A| ≤ n!·c^n. ∎

Formalization note. Matrix.det_le (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/AbsoluteValue.lean) is not in the closure of the frozen import. Finset.prod_le_prod is the ordered-monoid version (it needs MulLeftMono, which ℝ lacks), so use Finset.prod_le_prod₀. The script below was compiled as the proof of `theorem Submission.deformation_ipl_mwc_mil_abs_det_le : <frozen type>` under `import GMT.Ch06.Submission` in the contract scope (lake env lean; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
  intro n c A hA
  rw [Matrix.det_apply]
  calc |∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), Equiv.Perm.sign σ • ∏ i, A (σ i) i|
      ≤ ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), |Equiv.Perm.sign σ • ∏ i, A (σ i) i| :=
        Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ = ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∏ i, |A (σ i) i| := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
        rcases Int.units_eq_one_or (Equiv.Perm.sign σ) with h | h <;>
          simp [h, Finset.abs_prod]
    _ ≤ ∑ _σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), c ^ n := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun σ _ => ?_
        calc ∏ i, |A (σ i) i| ≤ ∏ _i : Fin n, c :=
              Finset.prod_le_prod₀ (fun i _ => abs_nonneg _) (fun i _ => hA _ _)
          _ = c ^ n := by simp
    _ = (n.factorial : ℝ) * c ^ n := by
        simp [Fintype.card_perm]
proof_key_steps: Leibniz expansion det A = Σ_σ sgn(σ)·Π_i A_{σ(i),i} (Matrix.det_apply).
Triangle inequality over the permutation sum (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs).
Each product Π_i |A_{σ(i),i}| ≤ c^n by monotonicity of products of nonnegative factors (Finset.prod_le_prod₀).
Summing n! = card(Perm (Fin n)) copies of c^n gives n!·c^n (Fintype.card_perm).

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree. Leibniz expansion, removal of permutation signs, nonnegative product monotonicity and permutation counting prove the stated bound. No extra assumption c ≥ 0 is needed: entry bounds suffice for nonempty products, and n = 0 gives equality. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: A.e. on an open set, a function agreeing with a coordinate of a Lipschitz map has the projected Fréchet derivative
subproblem.statement: Let k, Q ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k (ℝ^k = Eucl k) be open, C ≥ 0 (C : ℝ≥0), v : ℝ^k → ℝ^Q C-Lipschitz on Ω (LipschitzOnWith C v Ω), c ∈ Fin Q, and g : ℝ^k → ℝ any function with g(w) = EuclideanSpace.proj c (v(w)) for every w ∈ Ω. Then for Lebesgue-almost every w ∈ ℝ^k: if w ∈ Ω, then fderiv ℝ g w x = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w x) for every x ∈ ℝ^k. Here fderiv is Mathlib's Fréchet derivative, defined as 0 at points of non-differentiability; no regularity of g is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k Q : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)) (C : ℝ≥0) (v : Eucl k → Eucl Q) (c : Fin Q) (g : Eucl k → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → LipschitzOnWith C v Ω → EqOn g (fun w => EuclideanSpace.proj c (v w)) Ω → ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k)), w ∈ Ω → ∀ x : Eucl k, fderiv ℝ g w x = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6(a)–(b) of the supplied proof of the selected node (“Since Ω is an open neighbourhood of w on which ṽ^c = v^c, the two functions agree near w, so fderiv ℝ ṽ^c w = fderiv ℝ v^c w … By Rademacher's theorem on Ω … v is differentiable at λ-a.e. w ∈ Ω. At such w the chain rule for the continuous linear map EuclideanSpace.proj c gives fderiv ℝ v^c w = (EuclideanSpace.proj c).comp (fderiv ℝ v w)”). Here g replaces the McShane extension ṽ^c; only the equality g = v^c on Ω is used.

Notation. π := EuclideanSpace.proj c, a continuous linear map ℝ^Q →L[ℝ] ℝ; v^c := π ∘ v; λ := Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^k.

1. (Rademacher's theorem on Ω.) ℝ^k and ℝ^Q are finite-dimensional real normed spaces, λ is an additive Haar measure on ℝ^k, and v is C-Lipschitz on Ω. So Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem gives: for λ-a.e. w, if w ∈ Ω then v is differentiable within Ω at w. Fix such a w with w ∈ Ω, and fix x ∈ ℝ^k. It suffices to prove fderiv ℝ g w x = π(fderiv ℝ v w x) for this w and x.
2. (Within implies at.) Ω is open and w ∈ Ω, so Ω is a neighbourhood of w (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Differentiability within a neighbourhood of w is differentiability at w (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt). So v is differentiable at w, i.e. HasFDerivAt v (fderiv ℝ v w) w.
3. (Locality.) g and v^c agree on Ω, a neighbourhood of w, so g =ᶠ[𝓝 w] v^c (Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem). The Fréchet derivative depends only on the germ at w, so fderiv ℝ g w = fderiv ℝ v^c w (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). This holds whether or not g is differentiable at w.
4. (Chain rule.) A continuous linear map is its own derivative at every point (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt): HasFDerivAt π π (v w). Composing with step 2 (HasFDerivAt.comp) gives HasFDerivAt (π ∘ v) (π ∘L fderiv ℝ v w) w. Hence fderiv ℝ v^c w = π ∘L fderiv ℝ v w (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
5. (Evaluation.) By steps 3 and 4, fderiv ℝ g w x = (π ∘L fderiv ℝ v w) x = π(fderiv ℝ v w x) = EuclideanSpace.proj c (fderiv ℝ v w x). Here w was an arbitrary point of Ω in the conull set of step 1, and x was arbitrary. So the stated property holds for λ-a.e. w. ∎

Formalization note. The script below was compiled as the proof of `theorem Submission.deformation_ipl_mwc_mil_ae_fderiv_eq_proj : <frozen type>` under `import GMT.Ch06.Submission` in the contract scope (lake env lean; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
  intro k Q Ω C v c g hΩ hv hg
  filter_upwards [hv.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem (μ := volume)] with w hw hwΩ x
  have hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ v w := (hw hwΩ).differentiableAt (hΩ.mem_nhds hwΩ)
  have heq : g =ᶠ[𝓝 w] (fun w => EuclideanSpace.proj c (v w)) :=
    Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem (hΩ.mem_nhds hwΩ) hg
  rw [heq.fderiv_eq]
  have := ((EuclideanSpace.proj c).hasFDerivAt.comp w hd.hasFDerivAt).fderiv
  rw [show (fun w => EuclideanSpace.proj c (v w)) = (EuclideanSpace.proj c) ∘ v from rfl, this]
  rfl
proof_key_steps: Rademacher on Ω (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem): for a.e. w ∈ Ω, v is differentiable within Ω at w.
Ω open, so differentiability within Ω at w is differentiability at w.
g = proj_c ∘ v on the neighbourhood Ω of w, so fderiv ℝ g w = fderiv ℝ (proj_c ∘ v) w (EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
Chain rule for the continuous linear proj_c: fderiv ℝ (proj_c ∘ v) w = proj_c ∘L fderiv ℝ v w.
Evaluate at x: fderiv ℝ g w x = proj_c (fderiv ℝ v w x).

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose, including unrestricted g and the global a.e. implication on Ω. Rademacher supplies differentiability of v; openness upgrades within-differentiability and gives local equality with g. Locality and the continuous-linear projection chain rule then prove equality for every direction x. No unassumed regularity or circular dependency is used.

subproblem.title: Dominated convergence for integrands h_m·det A_m with uniformly bounded, a.e. convergent matrix entries
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (α : Type) [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (n : ℕ) (C : ℝ) (A : ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → α → ℝ) (A₀ : Fin n → Fin n → α → ℝ) (h : ℕ → α → ℝ) (h₀ H : α → ℝ), (∀ m t s, AEStronglyMeasurable (A m t s) μ) → (∀ m, AEStronglyMeasurable (h m) μ) → Integrable H μ → (∀ m t s x, |A m t s x| ≤ C) → (∀ᶠ m in atTop, ∀ x, |h m x| ≤ H x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun m => h m x) atTop (𝓝 (h₀ x))) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ t s, Tendsto (fun m => A m t s x) atTop (𝓝 (A₀ t s x))) → Tendsto (fun m => ∫ x, h m x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s => A m t s x) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, h₀ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s => A₀ t s x) ∂μ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4(a)–(c) and 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node: continuity of the determinant in the entries, the bound |det| ≤ n!·C^n for entries bounded by C, measurability via the Leibniz expansion, and dominated convergence via tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence. Here they are isolated as one statement about an arbitrary measure space. The selected node applies it to the left side φ·M[V^m] (with h_m = φ) and to every right-side summand V^m_0·C_q[V^m]·∂_{b(q)}φ (with h_m = (−1)^q·V^m_0·∂_{b(q)}φ).

Notation. F_m(x) := h_m(x)·det A_m(x), F(x) := h₀(x)·det A₀(x), K_n := n!·C^n, and g(x) := H(x)·K_n. S_n := Equiv.Perm (Fin n), and sgn(σ) ∈ {±1} is the sign of σ.

1. (Strategy.) Apply the dominated convergence theorem along the filter atTop on ℕ, which is countably generated: Mathlib's tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with bound g. Its hypotheses are:
(a) F_m is a.e.-strongly measurable for eventually all m;
(b) eventually in m, |F_m(x)| ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x;
(c) g is integrable;
(d) F_m(x) → F(x) for μ-a.e. x.
Its conclusion is ∫ F_m dμ → ∫ F dμ, which is the claim. The theorem needs no measurability of F; that follows from (a) and (d). Steps 2–5 verify (a)–(d).
2. ((a) Measurability, for every m.) By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply; the unit sgn(σ) acts as multiplication by the real number sgn(σ), via Units.smul_def and zsmul_eq_mul): det A_m(x) = Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} sgn(σ)·Π_{i ∈ Fin n} A_m(σ(i), i, x) for every x. Each A_m(σ(i), i, ·) is a.e.-strongly measurable by (i). Constants, finite products and finite sums of a.e.-strongly measurable real functions are a.e.-strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_const, AEStronglyMeasurable.mul, Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_fun_prod, Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_fun_sum). So x ↦ det A_m(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable, and so is F_m = h_m·det A_m, using (i) for h_m.
3. ((b) Domination.) By (iv), fix any m such that |h_m(x)| ≤ H(x) for every x; all sufficiently large m qualify. Fix x. By (iii), every entry of A_m(x) satisfies |A_m(t,s,x)| ≤ C, so the sibling lemma abs_det_le (with n, c := C and the matrix A_m(x)) gives |det A_m(x)| ≤ K_n. From 0 ≤ |h_m(x)| ≤ H(x) we get H(x) ≥ 0, and |det A_m(x)| ≥ 0. Multiplying the two inequalities (mul_le_mul) gives |F_m(x)| = |h_m(x)|·|det A_m(x)| ≤ H(x)·K_n = g(x). This holds for every x, hence μ-a.e., for all sufficiently large m.
4. ((c) Integrability.) g = H·K_n is a constant multiple of the μ-integrable H, so it is μ-integrable (Integrable.mul_const).
5. ((d) Pointwise convergence.) The conull sets in (v) and (vi) intersect in a conull set (filter_upwards). Fix x in it. By (vi), for each t the row (A_m(t,s,x))_s converges to (A₀(t,s,x))_s in the product topology. Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ carries the product topology, so A_m(x) → A₀(x) (tendsto_pi_nhds, applied twice). The determinant Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ is continuous, being a polynomial in the entries (Continuous.matrix_det applied to the identity map). Hence det A_m(x) → det A₀(x). By (v), h_m(x) → h₀(x), and products of convergent real sequences converge to the product of the limits (Tendsto.mul). So F_m(x) → F(x).
6. Steps 2–5 establish every hypothesis of dominated convergence, so ∫ h_m·det A_m dμ = ∫ F_m dμ → ∫ F dμ = ∫ h₀·det A₀ dμ. ∎ For n = 0 every determinant is 1 and K_0 = 1, and the argument is unchanged.

Formalization note. The script below was compiled as the proof of `theorem Submission.deformation_ipl_mwc_mil_tendsto_integral_mul_det : <frozen type>` under `import GMT.Ch06.Submission` in the contract scope, after the sibling deformation_ipl_mwc_mil_abs_det_le (lake env lean; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
  intro α _ μ n C A A₀ h h₀ H hAm hhm hH hAb hhb hhl hAl
  refine tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence
    (fun x => H x * ((n.factorial : ℝ) * C ^ n)) ?_ ?_ (hH.mul_const _) ?_
  · refine Eventually.of_forall fun m => (hhm m).mul ?_
    have : (fun x => Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun t s => A m t s x)) =
        fun x => ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ((Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) : ℝ) * ∏ i, A m (σ i) i x := by
      funext x
      rw [Matrix.det_apply]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
      rw [Units.smul_def, zsmul_eq_mul]
      rfl
    rw [this]
    refine Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_fun_sum _ fun σ _ => ?_
    exact aestronglyMeasurable_const.mul (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_fun_prod _ fun i _ => hAm m _ _)
  · filter_upwards [hhb] with m hm
    refine Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul]
    exact mul_le_mul (hm x)
      (Submission.deformation_ipl_mwc_mil_abs_det_le n C _ fun t s => hAb m t s x)
      (abs_nonneg _) ((abs_nonneg _).trans (hm x))
  · filter_upwards [hhl, hAl] with x hx1 hx2
    refine hx1.mul ?_
    have hc : Continuous (Matrix.det : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ) := continuous_id.matrix_det
    exact (hc.tendsto _).comp (tendsto_pi_nhds.2 fun t => tendsto_pi_nhds.2 fun s => hx2 t s)
proof_key_steps: Apply tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence along atTop with bound g = H·n!·C^n.
Measurability of h_m·det A_m via the Leibniz expansion into finite sums and products of a.e.-strongly measurable entries.
Domination: |det A_m(x)| ≤ n!·C^n by the sibling abs_det_le, and |h_m| ≤ H for all large m, so |h_m·det A_m| ≤ H·n!·C^n.
A.e. convergence: entrywise convergence gives matrix convergence (tendsto_pi_nhds), continuity of det gives det A_m(x) → det A₀(x), and Tendsto.mul with h_m(x) → h₀(x) finishes.
